subject: Materials Science
title: Addition vs Condensation Polymerization
description: A micro-lesson that makes Addition vs Condensation Polymerization usable.

hook.text: Two routes build a polymer chain — one keeps every atom, the other sheds water.

buildup.text: Addition polymerization opens double bonds — monomers click together, nothing lost.

discovery.text: Condensation polymerization joins monomers by releasing a small molecule, usually water.

twist.text: Nylon is condensation — each link releases one water molecule as it forms.

climax.text: Polyethylene is addition — no byproduct, just pure chain growth at industrial speed.

punchline.text: Add monomers or condense them — two roads to giant molecules.

quiz.question: What is released during condensation polymerization?
